baa_10y_spread.proxy_note: Moody's Baa corporate bond yield minus the 10Y Treasury -- a long-run investment-grade credit-risk-premium PROXY, not the literal ICE BofA IG OAS series this system quotes daily. Real history back to 1986. Useful for direction and episode timing (did credit broadly tighten/widen, and when); its magnitude runs tighter than IG OAS and far tighter than HY OAS, so never quote its level as if it were either.

history_digest.sentence: The 30-year Treasury yield (5.28%) first reached this level on Aug 17 and has been there on 42 of the 56 sessions since; before this run, the last time was Jul 2007, and only briefly (9 sessions between May 2006 and Jul 2007); it was last there routinely until Feb 2002. This run's high was 5.67% on Oct 7, last matched in Jul 2001. Today's reading is at or above the reading on 81 of every 100 days of the last 30 years, but about average (46th percentile) since 1977. Every reading in the 1980s was at or above today's 5.28%.

history_digest.sentence: The 10-year TIPS real yield (2.65%, dated 11-03) first reached this level on Sep 16 and has been there on 26 of the 34 sessions since; before this run, the last time was Nov 2008 (during the 2007-09 Global Financial Crisis). This run's high was 2.95% on Oct 5, last matched in Nov 2008. Today's reading is at or above the reading on 99 of every 100 days since 2003. But TIPS only exist since 2003: the Cleveland Fed's model real rate, back to 1982, puts real rates at the 80th percentile of the last 30 years and the 54th since 1982 — high against the last 30 years, about average since 1982.
